cleanIntro: The APX Carry is a micro pistol built around a removable serialised sub-chassis, and like its bigger brother it disassembles WITHOUT the trigger being pulled — the striker deactivation button does that job. The takedown control is a PIN that rotates a quarter turn, not a lever.

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber inspected
steps.action: Magazine out first, then look into the chamber and confirm it is empty. Beretta wants this before the Disassembly Pin is touched, and on a carry pistol that has been in a holster all week it is not a formality.
steps.aside: NOTICE: It is advisable to perform field stripping and assembly operations over a table to catch components should they drop.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine and ensure the pistol is unloaded by inspecting the barrel’s chamber.
steps.cite: Beretta APX Carry User Manual — ⛔ No form code is printed in this file's running header, unlike every other book in the drop; the document names itself "APX Carry" in its own text — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.28-30

steps.title: ⛔ Striker deactivation button — the pistol strips without a trigger pull
steps.action: Press the Striker Deactivation Button with a small punch or the tip of a ballpoint pen. This is a patented feature and it is the whole reason the APX Carry can be disassembled WITHOUT PULLING THE TRIGGER — Beretta's own capitals. Use it every time.
steps.aside: This means the pistol can be disassembled WITHOUT PULLING THE TRIGGER.
steps.quote: Depress the Striker Deactivation Button with a small punch or the tip of a ballpoint pen.
steps.cite: Beretta APX Carry User Manual — ⛔ No form code is printed in this file's running header, unlike every other book in the drop; the document names itself "APX Carry" in its own text — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.28-30

steps.title: Disassembly Pin a quarter turn COUNTER-clockwise
steps.action: Rotate the Disassembly Pin about a quarter turn counter-clockwise to disengage it from the barrel. A quarter turn, no more — this is a pin that rotates, not a lever that swings, and it is the difference between this pistol and the APX A1.
steps.quote: Rotate the Disassembly Pin approximately ¼ turn counterclockwise to disengage the Pin from the barrel.
steps.cite: Beretta APX Carry User Manual — ⛔ No form code is printed in this file's running header, unlike every other book in the drop; the document names itself "APX Carry" in its own text — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.28-30

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Run the slide forward and off the frame. Nothing is under tension yet.
steps.quote: Move the slide forward and remove it from the frame.
steps.cite: Beretta APX Carry User Manual — ⛔ No form code is printed in this file's running header, unlike every other book in the drop; the document names itself "APX Carry" in its own text — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.28-30

steps.title: Recoil spring out, then the barrel by its cam lug
steps.action: Lift the recoil spring assembly out of the slide, then grasp the barrel by the cam lug, tilt and remove it. Beretta says outright that nothing beyond this is required for routine maintenance.
steps.aside: NOTICE: No further disassembly is required for routine maintenance.
steps.quote: The recoil spring assembly can now be lifted out of the slide. Tilt the barrel by grasping the cam lug and remove the barrel from the slide.
steps.cite: Beretta APX Carry User Manual — ⛔ No form code is printed in this file's running header, unlike every other book in the drop; the document names itself "APX Carry" in its own text — FIELD STRIPPING, printed p.28-30

steps.title: Bore from the chamber end, all the way through before pulling back
steps.action: Oil on the bore brush, in from the chamber end, and push it ALL the way through before you draw it back — reversing a brush mid-bore is how bristles get folded over and dragged. Solvent first if it needs it, then patches until one emerges clean, then the locking lug, then a light oil everywhere.
steps.aside: Clean the barrel locking lug with a cloth soaked in gun oil. Lightly oil the entire barrel prior to reassembly.
steps.quote: Apply gun oil to a bore-cleaning brush. Insert the brush into the barrel from the chamber end and scrub the chamber and bore thoroughly. Make sure you pass the bore brush all the way through the barrel before pulling back through.
steps.cite: Beretta APX Carry User Manual — ⛔ No form code is printed in this file's running header, unlike every other book in the drop; the document names itself "APX Carry" in its own text — MAINTENANCE — BARREL

steps.title: Slide: breech face, extractor, rails, locking shoulders
steps.action: Oiled cloth over the slide with attention to the breech face, the extractor, the slide rails and the locking shoulders. NYLON brush only if it needs one — Beretta names the material, and a steel brush on a coated slide is not a small mistake.
steps.quote: Clean the slide with a cloth soaked in gun oil paying particular attention to the breech face, extractor, slide rails, locking shoulders. If necessary, use a NYLON cleaning brush.
steps.cite: Beretta APX Carry User Manual — ⛔ No form code is printed in this file's running header, unlike every other book in the drop; the document names itself "APX Carry" in its own text — MAINTENANCE — SLIDE

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly and the frame's three named areas
steps.action: Light oil on the spring guide assembly, nylon brush first if it is heavily fouled. On the frame, Beretta names exactly three areas: the cocking lever, the ejector and the slide rails. Dry them, then oil the rails lightly.
steps.aside: Using a cloth lightly soaked in gun oil, clean the areas of the cocking lever, the ejector, and the slide rails.
steps.quote: Lightly oil the spring guide assembly with gun oil. After extensive use it may be necessary to first clean these parts using a NYLON cleaning brush.
steps.cite: Beretta APX Carry User Manual — ⛔ No form code is printed in this file's running header, unlike every other book in the drop; the document names itself "APX Carry" in its own text — MAINTENANCE — RECOIL SPRING / FRAME

steps.title: ⛔ The magazine goes back DRY
steps.action: The follower must slide down freely under thumb pressure. Dry the internal walls with a cloth and leave NO oil in the magazine — oil in a magazine box collects the dust that eventually stops the follower, and Beretta says so flatly.
steps.aside: CAUTION: Do not apply excess oil. Accumulation of oil attracts dirt and dust, which can interfere with the functioning and reliability of the firearm.
steps.quote: Make sure the magazine is thoroughly clean and that the follower slides easily downward if pressed. Dry the internal walls of the magazine box with a cloth. Do not leave any oil in the magazine.
steps.cite: Beretta APX Carry User Manual — ⛔ No form code is printed in this file's running header, unlike every other book in the drop; the document names itself "APX Carry" in its own text — MAINTENANCE — MAGAZINE

deepSteps.title: Beretta publishes the grip-frame removal — read it through first
deepSteps.action: The APX Carry's serialised part is a sub-chassis, and Beretta publishes how to lift it out of the grip frame for maintenance or replacement. Start from a completed field strip. ⛔ Read the whole procedure before you begin — the book itself tells you to, because parts fall away in step 4 and there is no recovering an order you never observed.
deepSteps.aside: Beretta APX CARRY pistols have a sub-chassis that carries the serial number and firing mechanism.
deepSteps.quote: Step 1 Field strip the pistol following the “FIELD STRIPPING” instructions in this manual to remove the slide assembly (pages 28-30).
deepSteps.cite: Beretta APX Carry User Manual — ⛔ No form code is printed in this file's running header, unlike every other book in the drop; the document names itself "APX Carry" in its own text — GRIP FRAME REMOVAL, printed p.38-41

deepSteps.title: Disassembly Pin out, right to left
deepSteps.action: Push the Disassembly Pin out from right to left and put it somewhere it cannot roll away.
deepSteps.quote: Step 2 Push the Disassembly pin out from right to left and place it aside.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta APX Carry User Manual — ⛔ No form code is printed in this file's running header, unlike every other book in the drop; the document names itself "APX Carry" in its own text — GRIP FRAME REMOVAL, printed p.38-41

deepSteps.title: Cocking Lever Spring leg lifted, then the Rear Assembly Pin
deepSteps.action: With a small punch, lift the bent leg of the Cocking Lever Spring out of its retaining groove in the Rear Assembly Pin and let it rest ON the pin. Then, with the same punch, drive the Rear Assembly Pin out right to left. Letting the leg rest on the pin is the trick that makes this a one-punch job on a Carry.
deepSteps.quote: Step 3 With a small punch, lift the bent leg of the Cocking Lever Spring out of the retaining groove in the Rear Assembly Pin and let the leg of the spring rest on the pin. With the same punch, push the Rear Assembly Pin out of the frame from right to left and place it aside.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta APX Carry User Manual — ⛔ No form code is printed in this file's running header, unlike every other book in the drop; the document names itself "APX Carry" in its own text — GRIP FRAME REMOVAL, printed p.38-41

deepSteps.title: ⛔ Chassis out SLOWLY — pinch the trigger bar and slide catch
deepSteps.action: Depress the Striker Deactivation Button so the pin tips clear the inner walls, then raise the REAR of the chassis just enough to pinch the trigger bar (right) and the slide catch (left) against the sides of the chassis, and lift the assembly out. Before you set the grip frame down, take the slide catch spring out of its recess on the left of the frame. Pull the chassis out quickly and the trigger bar, slide catch and recoil spring support come away with it — and if you then rotate the chassis, the disconnect pin and trigger pin slide out of their holes too.
deepSteps.aside: Before setting the grip frame down, carefully remove the slide catch spring from its recess on the left side of the frame, and place it aside.
deepSteps.quote: CAUTION: If the chassis Is pulled out quickly the Trigger Bar, Slide Catch, and Recoil Spring Support may fall away from the chassis.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Brush in from the CHAMBER end and all the way through before pulling back
Solvent first if it needs it, then patches until one comes out clean
⛔ Never clean the barrel with the pistol assembled
Light oil on the whole barrel before it goes back

cleaning.name: SLIDE & BREECH FACE
tasks: Cloth or nylon brush on the breech face, extractor, rails and locking shoulders
Dry the slide surfaces, then lightly oil the guides

cleaning.name: RECOIL SPRING ASSEMBLY
tasks: Light gun oil on the spring guide assembly
Nylon brush first if it is heavily fouled — never a steel one

cleaning.name: FRAME & MAGAZINE
tasks: Fouling off the frame rails and the magazine well
Magazine lips and follower cleaned, then wiped with a lightly oiled rag
⛔ Never spray or apply oil to cartridges

reassembly: Barrel into the slide: tip it, muzzle end through the hole in the front of the slide, then lower the rear end into position.
Recoil spring assembly in with the large flat end engaged in the recess of the barrel cam lug.
⛔ Check the Disassembly Pin is in the UNLOCKED position, then install the slide assembly on the frame.
Muzzle safe, retract the slide SLOWLY and confirm the Disassembly Pin has returned to the “Locked” position.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: check the Disassembly Pin is in the UNLOCKED position before the slide goes on, then retract the slide SLOWLY with the muzzle safe and visually confirm the pin has returned to LOCKED. Cycle the slide several times, confirm it goes fully into battery, and check the trigger safety returns. ⛔ Never release a slide under spring pressure with the pin unlocked.
